headers.//: Scripts and styles are requested with a ?v=NNN that changes on every release, so the URL itself is the cache key and the bytes behind it never change. Caching them immutably turns a repeat visit from 84 revalidation round-trips into zero requests.
sw.js is fetched WITHOUT a version query and is how the app learns a new release exists. It must always be revalidated, so this rule deliberately follows the blanket js rule above to override it.

The entry document carries the ?v=NNN references, so it is how a client discovers a new release. cleanUrls redirects /index.html to /, so the bare root must be matched too — matching only /index.html leaves the document on Firebase's default max-age=3600 and delays every deploy by up to an hour.
manifest and offline data are fetched unversioned; revalidate so a content update is picked up.
